title: Data Residency & Tenant Isolation
summary: Control where tenant information is processed and retained, and prevent cross-tenant access across every derived artifact and operational surface.
overview: Residency governs permitted locations for processing, storage, replication, and access under an organization's applicable obligations. Tenant isolation governs separation between customers or organizational units. They intersect but are not interchangeable: two tenants in one region still need isolation, while one tenant's logs or backups can cross a residency boundary accidentally.

Map the complete data path, including prompts, embeddings, caches, traces, evaluation samples, support exports, and disaster-recovery copies. A regional database setting alone does not constrain model endpoints or telemetry. The enforcement design must account for identity, routing, storage partitions, encryption keys, and operator access.

production.poc: A proof of concept should use synthetic tenants and document every processor and artifact rather than assuming deployment region covers the whole workflow.
production.production: Production requires authenticated tenant context, location-aware routing, scoped retrieval, partitioned caches, controlled telemetry, and tested backup and failover behavior.
production.scale: Enterprise scale adds per-tenant policy variants, regional capacity planning, key ownership, support-access controls, migration procedures, and evidence that derived stores honor the same boundaries.

components.name: Tenant policy registry
components.role: Defines allowed processing regions, service classes, retention rules, and isolation requirements.

components.name: Identity-bound router
components.role: Derives tenant scope from authentication and selects only policy-compatible runtime and model endpoints.

components.name: Partitioned data services
components.role: Enforce tenant scope in relational, object, vector, cache, and workflow stores.

components.name: Regional telemetry pipeline
components.role: Applies minimization, access control, and permitted storage locations to traces and operational records.

components.name: Migration and recovery controller
components.role: Validates that replicas, backups, failover targets, and export jobs remain within approved policy.

flow.title: Resolve trusted tenant
flow.description: Bind the request to authenticated tenant identity and load the current policy version before retrieval or model selection.

flow.title: Choose permitted execution
flow.description: Filter runtime, model, and tool endpoints by processing-location and isolation requirements, failing closed if none qualify.

flow.title: Retrieve within boundaries
flow.description: Enforce tenant and resource predicates in every store, including caches and derived search indexes.

flow.title: Process and record minimally
flow.description: Send only necessary data and route logs, traces, and artifacts through compatible regional pipelines.

flow.title: Validate secondary paths
flow.description: Check backups, asynchronous jobs, evaluation exports, and operator access against the same tenant policy.

flow.title: Handle movement explicitly
flow.description: Perform migrations or disaster recovery only through approved destinations with verified cleanup and policy transition records.

useCase.title: Regional customer support assistant
useCase.situation: Illustrative architecture: A software provider serves customers whose approved processing regions and support-access rules differ.
useCase.problem: The main database is regional, but shared embeddings, global logs, and a fallback model can move customer content outside the intended boundary.
useCase.requirement: Apply the tenant's policy to every processing and derived-data path, including failure recovery.
useCase.architecture: A policy router selects regional runtimes and model endpoints; all stores require authenticated tenant keys and telemetry remains in the permitted pipeline.
useCase.failure: The preferred model endpoint fails; the router returns a controlled degraded response because the available alternative violates the tenant's location policy.
useCase.impact: Measure blocked cross-boundary attempts, data-path coverage, policy-compatible availability, and isolation test results; architecture controls alone do not establish legal compliance.

tradeoffs.benefit: Provides a stronger operational separation boundary.

tradeoffs.cost: Requires comprehensive enforcement and careful noisy-neighbor management.

tradeoffs.benefit: Preserves approved location boundaries during outages.
tradeoffs.cost: May reduce available recovery capacity or increase downtime.

failures.scenario: A semantic cache key omits tenant and policy version.
failures.detection: Isolation tests return a cached answer derived from another tenant's material.
failures.recovery: Disable the affected cache, investigate exposure, and rebuild entries with enforced tenant-aware keys.

failures.scenario: A disaster-recovery job targets an unapproved region.
failures.detection: Recovery preflight rejects the destination against tenant policy.
failures.recovery: Use an approved recovery target or report constrained availability without silently moving data.

mistakes.mistake: Checking only the primary database region.
mistakes.fix: Inventory models, embeddings, logs, backups, support tools, and evaluation exports.

mistakes.mistake: Trusting a tenant ID supplied in the prompt.
mistakes.fix: Derive tenant context from authenticated application claims and verify it downstream.
Enforce access and partition boundaries even when all stored data is encrypted.

whenToUse: A shared agent platform serves customers with different data-handling obligations.
Derived indexes and telemetry contain sensitive tenant information.
Availability planning must respect location and access constraints during failures.
whenNotToUse: All processed content is public and there is no meaningful tenant or location policy.
The proposed dependency cannot meet the required processing boundary.
A region label would be used as a substitute for legal and contractual assessment.
checklist: Inventory every primary, derived, operational, and recovery data path.
Bind tenant context to authenticated identity and propagate it through tools.
Constrain model and tool routing by current tenant policy.
Partition caches and indexes with enforced tenant and permission semantics.
Test cross-tenant reads, writes, exports, and noisy-neighbor behavior.
Verify backup, support-access, migration, and failover destinations.
Document policy-compatible degradation when no permitted endpoint is available.
